title: Only the Godhead is holy by nature and makes holy
english: …set it out. In one stroke he put forward the very heading we are now pursuing, and with it the Holy Spirit’s fellowship with God the Father in the great gifts and in the rebirth of baptism. He showed too that the name “God” is one and belongs equally to the Trinity, and that God the Father, God the Son and God the Spirit, when called upon, always work with equal power. Writing to the Corinthians, he declares: “But you were washed, but you were justified, but you were sanctified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God” (1 Corinthians 6:11).

That is why those who share in him, that is, those counted worthy to be sanctified, justified and made wise by him, are called “partakers of the Holy Spirit” (Hebrews 6:4), as the same apostle teaches the Hebrews. And to the Ephesians he writes: “In him you also, when you believed, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise” (Ephesians 1:13). It is plain that those who are sealed, that is, sanctified, share in him; they are not shared in. Indeed, if the Holy Spirit or the Son were a creature, what need would there be for a creature to sanctify and to fill up what is lacking, when God the Father had already sanctified enough? We who are created know that this anointing belongs to the uncreated one. So we do not supply sanctification from our own store, but we say, “May God sanctify you.”

I will go on to another proof, agreed by all and strong, after which not even those who have trained themselves in shamelessness will be able to keep it up. The Master of the universe, after giving his command about God the Father and himself without any qualifier, “baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son” (Matthew 28:19), did not simply go on, “and of the Spirit,” but added, “the Holy.” So he did not merely avoid naming him in a lower way; he named him in a higher one. For the Spirit is by nature what the self-complete hypostases are, which the one name signified, the name under which the Spirit himself was named with them. And in the same way the Holy Spirit is established as what the Father and his Son are in Godhead, and he was named together with them. That much, as the saying goes, is plain even to a blind man.

But this belongs to a fuller theology. Still, so that it may be readily believed that it is proper to the Godhead alone to be called holy and righteous, and to be so by nature, and further to sanctify and justify its own creatures, Scripture sings of the Father in the same terms. So the Son himself says in John, “Holy Father, keep them in your name” (John 17:11), and again, “Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth” (John 17:17), and once more, “Righteous Father” (John 17:25). So too the prophets: Ezekiel, “And let them know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them” (Ezekiel 20:12); David in the eleventh Psalm, “The Lord is righteous, and he has loved righteousness; his eyes have seen uprightness” (Psalm 11:7); and another, “And all who are sanctified are under your hands, and they are under you” (Deuteronomy 33:3). So too Paul, writing to the Thessalonians, “May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely” (1 Thessalonians 5:23); to the Romans, “It is God who justifies; who is the one who condemns?” (Romans 8:33-34); and to the Hebrews, “that the virgin may be holy in body and spirit” (1 Corinthians 7:34). He speaks as one for whom it is possible either that she, by turning of her own will, is not holy, or that she is made holy by virtue. By “spirit” he here means the settled state of the soul, and by “body” its practical activity, as Isaiah prophesies: “And those who go astray in spirit will come to understanding” (Isaiah 29:24), that is, those who go astray in deed or in settled state.

And of the Son, as when he is praised, “One is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ”; and as the Acts say, “They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One” (Acts 7:52); and as Peter said, “Christ died for sinners, the righteous for the unrighteous” (1 Peter 3:18). From such oracles, then, they ought, if they wished to act justly, to be led on to praising the Spirit as God. This they do not do. Instead they assert that the angels were not sanctified and yet are holy…

added_allusions.reason: “One is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ” is the liturgical acclamation before Communion; its second half echoes “one Lord Jesus Christ” in 1 Corinthians 8:6. Not cited inline.

translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

The old English was a garbled draft ('perhaps belongs to the Trinity', 'the sixth [thing]', 'Father, judge', a sentence broken off at 'the Pa—', the printed line number '[about 60]'). Four abbreviated references written out; Romans 8:33 -> 8:33-34; Deuteronomy 33:3 and Acts 7:52 added; Greek Psalm 10 given as the eleventh; bracket fillers removed.
